modelingNotes: Camp North End: 201 Camp Road — procedural, CC0-1.0. bun generators/clt-cne-201-camp-road.ts

The north-east half of the Army Quartermaster Corps' Building No. 5 (1941–43), the longest of the depot's south warehouses (1,200 ft and ten monitors when whole, as the 2016 lidar still shows it); its middle bay is `clt-cne-701-keswick` and its south-west end was taken down for Kinship East and the parking garage. Renovated as offices in 2021. A one-storey red-brick box 55 × 184 m, taller than its neighbours (9.8 m to the deck), five corrugated-metal clerestory monitors across its width at 36.6 m spacing, low brick annexes and a canopy in the recesses of its north-west side, a loading platform under a canopy along the railway on the south-east.
Identity: the long red brick box with five evenly spaced monitors across its white roof, the tallest of the south warehouses.

Evidence: - OSM: the outline way/324608496 and its 17 parts: monitors way/835808920, 835808923, 835808925, 835808928, 835808931 (height 10.4); main roof 835808919, 835808922, 835808924, 835808927, 835808930, 835808932 (8.2); the west bump 835808926 (7.5); annexes and canopy 835808918, 835808929, 835844005, 1108286803 (5.2); the railway platform 835808921 (1). - Lidar, USGS 3DEP NC Phase 4 Mecklenburg 2016, 1 m (measured, NAVD88): ground 227.5–228.6, mostly 228.1 (y = 0 is 227.5, at the north-east end); deck 237.3 (9.8 m); monitors 240.1 (12.6 m), each 14 m wide; annexes, canopy and the railway canopy 234.0 (6.5 m); the bump 235.1 (7.6 m). OSM's heights are each about 1.5 m low; the lidar is followed. - C-M Historic Landmarks Commission survey report (2017, landmarkscommission.org/wp-content/uploads/2017/06/Ford-Motor-Co-Plant-SR.pdf), Buildings Nos. 4–6 (published): brick in common bond, 180 ft wide, corrugated-metal clerestory monitors across the width, "ten monitors on building No. 5", which "sprawls back 1200 feet". - Mecklenburg County tax parcel 07903C99 (CAMP 201 PROPERTY OWNER LP): built 1943, face brick. Camp North End leasing brochure (2021, camp.nc): "201 Camp Road", 115,000 sq ft, Phase 2. - USGS NAIP orthophoto (public domain): the white roofs, rust-streaked, the dark annex roofs and canopies on the north-west side.

No licensed photo of this building was found (Commons, Openverse and Mapillary have nothing inside the campus). So: - the brick, the monitors' cladding and glazing and the plinth are taken from its siblings, 301 Camp Road (Commons photos) and 1720 Statesville Avenue (Mapillary) — estimated; - the windows are invented: two tiers on the north-west and north-east faces, as on 701 Keswick's end wall (the one partial photo of Building No. 5, in File:Free_Range_Brewing_Camp_North_End_in_the_301_Camp_building_Early_June_2025.jpg, City Dweller 2, CC BY-SA 4.0), loading doors along the railway; - the annexes' walls are drawn in the same brick.
Frame and kit: `clt-cne-301-camp-road.ts`. y along the long axis (bearing 39.34°), placement bearing 39.34; origin at the outline's centroid, lng −80.8323195, lat 35.2463603.
